blocks.text: My name is Claire Moretti, and for seven years, I believed I was married to a man who simply didn’t know how to love.
Vincent Moretti was a successful Chicago businessman. He wore expensive suits, drove luxury cars, and commanded respect wherever he went.
To everyone else, he was charming, intelligent, and powerful.
He rarely kissed me without being reminded. He never remembered our anniversary without a calendar notification. And whenever I brought up having children, he always had another excuse.
Sophia had been my closest friend since college. When her marriage collapsed, she had nowhere to go, so I invited her to stay in our guest suite.
I cooked for her, listened to her cry, and helped her rebuild her life.
He made sure she had everything she needed. He paid for her appointments and even arranged transportation when she needed to visit doctors.
I couldn’t have been more wrong. The hospital room Three months ago, Sophia told me she was pregnant.
“I don’t know what I’m going to do, Claire.”
I hugged her and promised she wouldn’t face anything alone.
She refused to tell me who the father was.
“I’ll explain everything when I’m ready,” she whispered.
Then, one Thursday afternoon, Sophia was admitted to the hospital because of complications with her pregnancy.
“Claire, could you bring me that cheesecake from the bakery on Michigan Avenue? The one with strawberries?”
I picked up the cheesecake and hurried back to the hospital.
But when I reached her room, I heard Vincent’s voice.
My fingers tightened around the cake box.
“I only married her because she was useful,” he continued. “She trusted me completely. That made everything easier.”
“What happens when she finds out about us?”
“Emily is handling everything. Once the divorce papers are ready, Claire will have no choice but to leave. The house, the company shares, everything will stay with me.”
Then I looked through the slightly open door.
Vincent was kneeling beside Sophia’s bed, gently resting his hand on her stomach.
I wanted to storm inside and demand answers.
Instead, I placed the cheesecake on the hallway table and walked away.
Two weeks earlier, I’d taken a pregnancy test after feeling unusually exhausted.
I hadn’t told Vincent because I wanted to surprise him.
Now I was beginning to understand why he had always found reasons to postpone having children.
Perhaps he never wanted a family with me.
Perhaps he had been waiting for someone else. The first phone call The following morning, I contacted a divorce attorney named Rebecca Collins.
When I finished, she asked one question.
“Claire, do you have any idea how your husband’s company is structured?”
“Not really. Vincent handles all the business decisions.”
“That’s exactly what concerns me. Bring every document you can find. Especially anything related to your marriage, property, and financial arrangements.”
That afternoon, I searched through our home office.
Inside a locked filing cabinet, I discovered documents I had never seen before.
There were company registration papers, financial statements, and an agreement bearing my signature.
According to the paperwork, I had supposedly agreed to transfer my interest in a family investment trust to Vincent.
Vincent had told me he needed my signature on some routine tax documents.
I’d signed several pages without reading every line.
Rebecca examined the documents the next morning.
“Claire, this may be more serious than infidelity. We need to establish whether your signature was obtained through deception and whether the transfer was legally valid.”
She also advised me not to confront Vincent until we understood the financial situation.
For the first time in seven years, I stopped trusting my husband. Emily’s little secret Two days later, I received a message from Emily.
“Claire, we need to talk. Please don’t make this difficult.”
She arrived wearing a cream-colored coat and carrying an expensive handbag.
“Vincent wants to separate,” she announced.
“He’s unhappy. Sophia makes him happy. You should accept that.”
“There’s something you should understand. Vincent has been planning this for a long time. You were never supposed to become part of his future.”
“Some people are better at being wives than being mothers.”
Her words struck harder than she could imagine.
She knew how much Vincent’s repeated excuses had hurt me.
And she was enjoying every second of it.
Before leaving, she placed an envelope on the table.
“These are the preliminary divorce papers. Sign them, and you can walk away with your dignity.”
“Tell Vincent I’ll need time to review everything.”
Her smile disappeared. The secret behind Sophia’s pregnancy That evening, Rebecca called.
She had discovered something unusual while reviewing the documents I had provided.
The investment trust Vincent was trying to transfer had originally belonged to my late grandmother.
